:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0), (1,0)$ and $(0,2),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
\displaystyle{\oint\limits_{C}\cos{y}\,\mathrm{d}x+x\sin{y}\,\mathrm{d}y}= \iint\limits_D f(x,y) \,\textrm d A,
$$

where $C$ is traversed counterclockwise. Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
\oint\limits_{C} P\,\mathrm{d}x + Q\,\mathrm{d}y 
= \iint\limits_D \left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)\,\textrm d A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/a7/a78a98750e3203760d27daaebd42852198538935e2c3777a0b8a8c85d1bb0901.png)

We have that $P(x,y)= \cos{y}$ and $Q(x,y)= x\sin{y}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dx+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y) = 2\sin{y}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$

We have that $P(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy).$ Therefore,

$$

$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dx-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-(-2y)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2y(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
